business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Subtitle Transcription and AI Voice Cloning Studio

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Arab Republic of Egypt (Jumhuriyyat Misr al-Arabiyya)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt, a unitary national jurisdiction (no sub-state fiscal autonomy) for Limited Liability Company incorporation, administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law — codified Napoleonic tradition (Civil Code and Commercial Code), with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution; corporate matters administerively unitary
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt – United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1995)
Egypt – India DTAA and investment protection instruments (Indian tax treaty in application since 1985)
Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital (League of Arab States framework; Egypt a party)
Treaty Establishing the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA; Egypt a founding member)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 concerning Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Laws No. 36 of 2014, No. 8 of 2015, No. 78 of 2016, No. 154 of 2019, and No. 155 of 2019, together with its Executive Regulations; Cabinet Decree No. 2790 of 2019 on Beneficial Ownership registers; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (shareholding and control disclosure provisions); Commercial Register Law No. 34 of 1976; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT instructions; GAFI mandatory UBO disclosure form under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the UBO register is maintained by GAFI/Unified Commercial Registry and supervised by the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); beneficial ownership filings are non-public and protected by statutory bank secrecy and confidentiality duties, while being fully accessible to supervisory and law-enforcement authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified certificate of good standing and corporate extract for a foreign corporate shareholder, or notarized passport bio-photocopies for natural-person founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry, Chamber of Commerce or public notary competent in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention entered into force on 14 December 2021); for non-convention countries, Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original signed shareholders' resolution authorizing formation of the Egyptian LLC, the appointment of its first manager(s), and the resolution's UBO disclosure schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / corporate body of the founding shareholder at its foreign registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the signatory's capacity and signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutional documents (memorandum and articles of association / charter) of each corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry authority of the founder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-funds solvency letter covering the cash or in-kind subscriptions to the LLC's registered capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign or Egyptian banking institution maintaining the founder's relationship account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer notarization followed by Apostille/Consular Legalization; for domestic banks, authentication per Central Bank of Egypt procedures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney in favor of the resident Egyptian counsel completing the incorporation and name-reservation process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the founder's country or the Egyptian Consulate where the founder resides
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization and, upon arrival in Egypt, registration with the Egyptian Notary Public Authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Law No. 80/2002 as amended: every director, manager, shareholder and beneficial owner must be screened against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the Egyptian National Terrorism List published under Law No. 8 of 2015, the Egyptian FIU's internal watchlist, and, where the LLC or its payment rails have a US nexus, the OFAC SDN list. Politically Exposed Persons are categorized per FATF Guidance and require senior management approval, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, and continuous transaction monitoring; suspicion is reportable to the Egyptian FIU within the statutory window of five business days, and bank signature cards are issued only after completion of the banks' CDD questionnaires.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Investor Services Portal — company name availability module of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (www.gafi.gov.eg), mirrored in the Unified Commercial Registry Database of the Ministry of Justice's Commercial Registry Administration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official LLC name must be composed in Arabic script and must clearly include the legal form suffix for limited liability company. A parallel Latin transliteration may be presented in English contract documents, provided it is the phonetic rendering of the Arabic name and does not create a variation intended to circumvent clearance. The name may not be identical, deceptively similar, or phonetically confusing with any name or distinctive trademark already recorded in the Commercial Register or the Egyptian trademark register of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; Arabic-name uniqueness is determinative.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying emanation, sponsorship, or privilege of the Egyptian State, the Armed Forces, intelligence, presidency, ministries, municipalities or public administration (e.g., 'National', 'Governmental', 'Military', 'Presidential', 'Official', 'Police', 'Army')

Monetary and fiduciary regulated tokens such as 'Bank', 'Central', 'Insurance', 'Guarantee', 'Reinsurance', 'Takaful', or 'Trust' — requiring prior approval of the Central Bank of Egypt or the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority
Names of foreign sovereigns, states, international organizations, or formulations misrepresenting official affiliation ('United Nations', 'World Bank', 'International Monetary Fund')
Religious, sectarian, or nobility insignia, and terms offensive to public morality or public order
A name already rejected within the current rolling register or identical or confusingly similar to a domain/brand for which a prior ministerial objection is recorded
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an electronic refusal notice in the GAFI portal, the applicant (or the attorney with notarized power) must file a written administrative appeal with the Commercial Registry's First Instance examination unit within 30 days from refusal, attaching the negative clearance decision, three substitute names, and legal grounds showing distinctiveness; the examination unit must decide within 15 business days. A negative second-level decision may be escalated to the GAFI Vice Chairman for Investment Services. In parallel, the reserved name may be renewed once for an additional 60-day window before the incorporation dossier is finalized. A rejected name may be re-submitted with a different type-fragment or activity suffix where the objection relates only to sector-sensitive wording.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mail-forwarding or virtual address is not permissible as the sole registered office of the LLC under Companies Law No. 159/1981 and Investment Law No. 72/2017; the company must maintain a physical, real, and permanently accessible seat in Egypt — either leased premises, a co-working or serviced-office tenancy within a licensed commercial tower, or a private residence formally approved by the municipal governorate. For a low-footprint AI post-production subtitle studio, a serviced office is acceptable for registration purposes and is verified at issuance of the business-operation license; the governing lease term shall not be less than one year.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is approximately 20% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Unified Commercial Registry and tax administration within the first full fiscal year, rising to approximately 35% if the studio invoices related media-production companies without maintaining substantive local presence. Commercial-registry and social-insurance sampling inspections add modest non-inspection contact risk; full remote operation without any on-site workstation materially increases audit flags.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and reservation (GAFI / Unified Commercial Registry database)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee item under Commercial Register Law No. 34 of 1976 schedule and GAFI service pricing circular

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the LLC's incorporation contract (memorandum of association) before the Notary Public Authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Justice, Notary Public Authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary tariff and stamp-duty scale applicable to limited-liability company formation documents under the Egyptian Civil Code and Law No. 159/1981; rounded per current published rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Unified commercial registry filing and issuance of the commercial registration certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI / Unified Commercial Registry (Ministry of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration-fee table under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Commercial Register Law No. 34 of 1976, including e-payment surcharge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax identification registration — tax card and VAT/withholding registration at the Egyptian Tax Authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No issuance fee; administrative courier and certified-copy costs at official tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register initial filing (UBO statement and signatory declarations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI in coordination with the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit under Law No. 154 of 2019
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative filing fee for UBO schedules integrated into the e-incorporation dossier; official tariff subject to annual decree

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation and transliteration of the standardized corporate pack (power of attorney stamps, bank KYC forms)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed translator registered with the Egyptian Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per certified page (average 0.75 USD/line equivalent) and Chamber of Commerce attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign founding documents (bundle of five originals and two certified copies each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section and consulates of document-origin states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document apostille/authentication tariffs plus consular legalization fee where the origin state is not a Hague Convention member

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local incorporation counsel and corporate-secretary onboarding (drafting Arabic AOA, manager appointment, shareholder register, compliance roadmap)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Egyptian law firm engaged by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a foreign-owned non-resident LLC incorporation package, including interlocking with bank and license preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening logistics — notarized bank signature cards, KYC/UBO attestation and manager specimen signatures (USD/EUR and EGP accounts; funding via Stripe and Wise)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank account provider and notary for board-signature authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for signature-authentication and CDD processing; no incorporation-linked levy; market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Round-trip currency variance and contingency allowance on government tariffs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Funding pool retained by the founder's counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Approximately 5% buffer over statutory and quoted tariffs to absorb EGP/USD fluctuation between payment milestones; standard market practice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Articles 1-32 for Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, Articles 60-96; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations, where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop; Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract), Company Incorporation Application (talab taasees al-sharikah), and the Commercial Register application; the official certificate issued upon registration is the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Qayd).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. The subscribed share capital is divided into equal nominal shares and fully paid within the period specified in the Articles of Association. The paid-up portion must be deposited in a temporary bank account with a licensed Egyptian bank, and the bank's deposit certificate is filed with GAFI before commercial registration is granted. There is no separate escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, in accordance with Article 12 of the Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the founding Articles of Association of [EG_LLC], that the duly incorporated Limited Liability Company hereby (1) adopts and confirms the Articles of Association as executed before the GAFI-certified notary; (2) acknowledges subscription of the entire share capital, split equally among the founding members and divided into equal shares; (3) confirms the registered office at [address in Cairo/Egypt] and authorizes the manager to affix the company's name and number to all corporate records; (4) mandates execution and deposit of the incorporation file with GAFI and the Commercial Registry; and (5) appoints [Name], [Name], and [Name] as signatories/managers to exercise all powers in accordance with law. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Form Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop via Sharikaty electronic portal (www.sharikaty.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application to reserve the company name in Arabic and transliterated English, verify the proposed legal form, and confirm that the intended post-production and AI dubbing business is lawful under the approved commercial code ISIC 5912. Pay the name reservation fee through the electronic portal and download the name availability certificate. If any founder acts through an attorney, also upload the notarized power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in Arabic and English
Copy of national ID or passport for each founding member
Authorization letter or power of attorney if a representative signs
Proof of name reservation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of similarity or noncompliance, file a fresh name reservation with a new name or submit a written objection to GAFI's legal department. GAFI will issue its decision within seven working days, or the applicant may initiate the administrative appeal process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Execute, and Notarize Articles of Association with Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Documentation Office), operating under Law No. 68 of 1947
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association in Arabic, including company name, business purpose, address, capital structure, shareholding percentages, manager names and powers, and registered office. Each founding member must personally appear before an Egyptian public notary or act through a notarized power of attorney. Before notarization, open a temporary bank account in Egypt with the intended paid-up capital and obtain the capital deposit certificate. The notary will attest signatures and authenticate the incorporation deed; the capital deposit certificate is attached as an annex to the deed.
required_dossiers: Four original copies of the Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate issued by a licensed Egyptian bank
Valid national IDs, passports, or commercial registration certificates of founders
Residency or visa documents for foreign founders
Notarized power of attorney if a representative appears
Tax identification numbers of founder entities, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial office returns the file for correction, revise and resubmit within fifteen days. If the legal reason for refusal is doubtful, request a reasoned written decision and submit it, together with a legal memorandum, to the GAFI dispute settlement unit for guidance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with GAFI and Obtain Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop and the Commercial Registry Office of the relevant Egyptian governorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete notarized incorporation file electronically or physically to GAFI, including the capital deposit certificate, notarized Articles of Association, board resolution appointing managers, and identification documents. GAFI verifies the file, recommends the issuance of the Commercial Registration certificate, and the Commercial Registry issues the commercial registration number. Simultaneously initiate the criminal record clearance process for all managers and the application for the company tax card at the Egyptian Tax Authority.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate
Power of attorney and founding members' identification
Commercial Register application forms
Criminal record extracts for all managers authorized to sign
Board resolution appointing the manager or general manager
Draft company incorporation summary and statutory declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a query or conditional approval, remedy the flagged deficiencies by filing an amending deed or supplementary statement and pay the re-review fee. A formal refusal may be appealed before the GAFI internal grievance committee under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Incorporation Notice and Complete Court Commercial Registry Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Journal (Al-Waqai Al-Masria), GAFI, and the competent Economic Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration is granted, arrange the mandatory publication of the incorporation notice and a summary of the Articles of Association in the Official Journal within the statutory period. Deliver the GAFI approval letter, the commercial registration certificate, and the notarized deed to the competent economic court's commercial registry for final indexing. Obtain certified copies of the publication page and the court registration mark to complete the legal formation condition.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
GAFI incorporation approval letter
Mandatory publication request form
Payment receipts for official journal and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed due to the Official Journal printing schedule, request a late publication certificate and pay the administrative late fee. For court registry delays, a written filing reminder may be submitted, and the company may seek an expedited judicial order if the registry remains inactive beyond twenty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Insurance Registration, and Corporate Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Social Solidarity Social Insurance Office, and a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within sixty days from commercial registration, register the company with the ETA for corporate income tax, value added tax, and wage tax payroll accounts. Apply for the official tax card and tax file number. Register the company as an employer at the social insurance office if staff are hired. Open the permanent corporate operating bank account at the CBE-licensed bank, transfer the provisional paid-up capital from the temporary deposit account into the operating account, and complete the final specimen signature card and KYC documentation.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
GAFI incorporation approval letter
Tax card application form and questionnaire
Board resolution appointing certain signatories
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership contract)
Valid IDs and passports of the signatories
Capital deposit certificate and provisional bank records
Social insurance declaration form if employing staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA delays issuance of the tax card, submit a formal complaint to the ETA customer services unit and request a supervisor review; the tax card will normally issue within five working days. If the bank rejects or delays the account opening for AML/KYC reasons, resubmit the file with enhanced due diligence, source of wealth statements, and the company's full incorporation certificate to satisfy the bank's compliance officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing board if the entity operates exclusively as an AI subtitle transcription, dubbing, and post-production studio in leased office premises; a media operations notification may otherwise be required by the Supreme Council of Media Regulation if it distributes content in Egypt. For any physical studio facility, GAFI One-Stop Shop coordinates with the relevant civil defense and municipal authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operational or manufacturing permit is required for a digital post-production and automated subtitle dubbing studio under ISIC 5912. If physical set construction or high-voltage broadcast equipment is deployed, an electrical installation conformity certificate from the Ministry of Electricity and the local district municipal license may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C low-risk service activity; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report requirement. A simple environmental registration form or self-monitoring notice may be filed with the EEAA branch office when commencing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the studio's operations. Sewage must be discharged into the municipal network in compliance with Law No. 93 of 1962 and its executive regulations; any negligible VOC emissions from printing, solvents, or server cooling must remain below occupational exposure limits set under Law No. 12 of 2003. E-waste from electronic equipment must be handled through an EEAA-approved licensed waste recycler in accordance with Law No. 202 of 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The studio must obtain a fire safety certificate from the General Department of Civil Defense after inspection of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and electrical wiring. A structural load clearance certificate for the leased or owned premises must also be issued by an accredited engineering office and verified by the municipal building administration. Additionally, the workplace registration and occupational safety and health clearance must be obtained from the Ministry of Manpower under Law No. 12 of 2003, including a first-aid cabinet, fire warden training, and ergonomic workstation compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) (مصلحة الضرائب المصرية); public e-portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-tax clearance portal: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; combined incorporation and tax registration is available through the GAFI one-stop-shop (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the LLC at the Commercial Registry through GAFI's one-stop-shop under Company Law 159/1981 as amended (no minimum capital; 100% foreign ownership permitted), obtaining the commercial register extract and incorporation certificate. Step 2: File tax registration forms with the competent ETA tax office pursuant to Tax Procedures Law No. 8 of 2010 within 30 days of commencing activity, attaching the incorporation deed, board resolution, passports/IDs of managers, authorized signatories, lease/address proof and business description; the ETA then issues the Tax Card (Bitāqa Ḍarībiyya) and the Tax Registration Number (TIN - tax office code + serial number). Step 3: Register for VAT under Law 67/2016 within 60 days after the registered person exceeds the EGP 500,000 annual turnover threshold, or immediately for voluntary registration, obtaining a separate VAT registration certificate. Step 4: Register as an employer for salary tax and withholding tax (Form 2) and obtain the digital signature certificate required for e-Tax portal access and e-invoicing API authentication. Step 5: Obtain the exporter/customs code through the electronic customs platform and open an Egyptian bank account (EGP and FX) with a CBE-authorized bank, which is required for export proceeds repatriation and for evidencing the inward remittance in export zero-rating claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the EG LLC is a resident company taxed on worldwide net income under Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 30/2023, at 15% on annual taxable profits up to EGP 120 million and 22.5% on the excess. Distributions to a foreign corporate parent are generally subject to a 10% Egyptian withholding tax (gross), while royalties, management fees and technical service fees paid offshore are subject to a 20% withholding tax. A non-resident without a permanent establishment is taxed only on Egypt-source income. No pass-through, partnership or territorial participation exemption is available for an LLC; the export service income remains fully within the Egyptian CIT base.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch classification election. Available statutory elections include: (i) adoption of a non-calendar fiscal year subject to ETA approval; (ii) optional small/micro business simplified cash-basis and turnover-rate taxation for eligible SMEs; (iii) voluntary VAT registration for sub-threshold businesses and the election to recover VAT via refund rather than credit; (iv) transfer-pricing method selection under the best-method rule (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split) and optional unilateral, bilateral or multilateral Advance Pricing Agreements with the ETA under Decree 320/2019; (v) ordinary foreign tax credit with no basket election; (vi) indefinite carry-forward of tax losses with no carry-back, subject to ownership continuity rules; thin-capitalization rules disallow interest on debt exceeding a 4:1 debt-to-equity ratio, and hybrid financing instruments may be recharacterized by the ETA under general anti-abuse principles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended (including Law No. 3 of 2017 which raised the standard rate to 14%); a separate selective Table Tax applies on certain luxury goods; no GST or sales-and-use tax regime exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover of supplies; mandatory VAT registration is required within 60 days after the threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold; taxpayers below the threshold may use the simplified small-taxpayer procedure and are not immediately subject to the e-invoicing mandate until integrated by ETA decree.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing is compulsory for VAT-registered businesses. Invoices must be issued electronically in JSON or XML, digitally signed (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256 hash), transmitted to the ETA portal (https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg) or through certified ERP/API integrations, and must receive an ETA acceptance code after real-time validation. Invoices must also display a QR code containing the invoice digest data. The standard B2B submission window is within 24 hours of issuance; rejected invoices are deemed non-issued and may be corrected only by credit/debit notes. The e-receipt regime (real-time B2C transmission) has been rolled out in phases since July 2022. Enforcement of e-invoicing now covers all VAT registrants; failure to transmit and clear invoices triggers fines under Law 67/2016 and the e-invoicing decrees.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT under Article 19 of Law 67/2016 applies to: (i) exports of goods with physical removal from Egypt evidenced by a customs export declaration; (ii) exports of services, including AI subtitle transcription, localization, dubbing and voice-cloning services performed in Egypt but supplied to a non-resident customer, where the service is consumed or benefitted from wholly outside Egypt, the deliverables are delivered offshore through secure digital transfer, the purchaser does not exploit the output in Egypt, and consideration is received in freely convertible foreign currency; (iii) supplies to free zones for final consumption abroad; and (iv) international transport-related supplies. The exporter must hold a valid VAT registration and exporter code and must substantiate the foreign supply with contemporaneous legal, technical and banking documentation. The right to use or exploit the exported service output must remain outside Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed export contract / Statement of Work (ISIC 5912 subtitling and AI dubbing deliverables) identifying the non-resident counterparty and the offshore use of deliverables
Commercial invoice stating 'VAT 0% - export supply' and bearing the ETA-validated e-invoice code and QR

Customs Export Declaration (Bayan) / electronic SAD issued through the NAFEZA platform for any physical component, or the digital service delivery report with platform logs, checksums, timestamps and server information for intangible AI deliverables
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill for physical media, or digital handover certificate with foreign delivery evidence for AI subtitle files
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Egyptian bank, or SWIFT MT103, evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Egyptian bank statement showing the foreign-currency credit, together with the CBE export contract summary when required by the authorized bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA audits export zero-rating claims through its transfer-pricing unit and may recharacterize a domestic-linked or fictitious offshore delivery as a taxable supply at 14%, disallow the refund, and impose: (i) assessment of the evaded VAT with an additional tax equal to the evaded amount; (ii) a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% on overdue tax under long-standing ETA practice aligned with Law 91/2005; (iii) fixed administrative fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 per non-compliant invoice or record, doubling on recidivism; (iv) higher fines and non-deductibility consequences for missing e-invoice clearance codes; (v) criminal liability for directors and managers for intentional fraudulent export documentation, with imprisonment and monetary penalties ranging from double to triple the evaded tax; and (vi) retrospective clawback of refunds for open years up to the 5-year statute of limitations, in addition to Central Bank of Egypt exchange-control penalties for failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is classified as a partially convertible currency with a unified market-driven exchange rate since the 2022 liberalization. Current account transactions benefiting bona fide trade in services (including post-production and AI-based subtitling services) are generally permitted, subject to documentary verification of the underlying contract, tax registration, and the submission of a valid invoice or license agreement. Profit remittances and dividend transfers to non-resident shareholders are treated as capital account transactions: they require (i) audited annual financial statements, (ii) a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority, (iii) a Board of Directors resolution authorizing the distribution, and (iv) a foreign currency availability declaration from the commercial bank. The main hurdle is not a statutory cap but the operational allocation of foreign currency liquidity within the authorized bank; banks may apply an administrative queue for USD conversion. Effective repatriation typically takes 5-10 business days once the documentary file is complete.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Circular No. 548/2022 and subsequent monetary policy notices, Egyptian exporters must receive export proceeds in a licensed Egyptian bank within 180 days from the bill of lading/shipping date, extendable to 240 days for service industries with documented milestone billing. The exporter may retain 100% of the foreign currency in an Egyptian Foreign Currency Account or debit it against future import obligations; there is no mandatory conversion to EGP for the export of post-production services. If the exporter converts the proceeds to EGP, conversion must be made at the prevailing market exchange rate on the date of crediting. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window subjects the exporter to CBE penalties, exclusion from subsidized finance facilities, and denial of the annual tax certificate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW. Egypt enforces CBE Law No. 18/2019 on Payment Services and E-Commerce, requiring any entity that issues e-money, executes payment account acquisition, or facilitates cross-border settlement to be a CBE-licensed payment institution with a local branch. Offshore EMI digital wallets (e.g., Wise, Stripe operating as EMI, Revolut) cannot hold an Egyptian correspondent account or directly clear EGP; they may only be engaged as a front-end aggregation layer through CBE-licensed local payment gateways such as PaySky, Fawry, or Amazon Payment Services. For the EG_LLC payout flow, the optimal compliant route is: offshore EMI collects global client invoices in USD/EUR -> EMI wires to the LLC's Egyptian USD operational account via SWIFT MT103 using the purpose code 'P-2' or 'D-2' as remittance for services rendered. Direct EGP custody on an offshore EMI is prohibited and would expose the LLC to non-declared currency transaction penalties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002 and the CBE Know-Your-Customer Rules mandate face-to-face verification for corporate account opening. At least one director who is a natural person or a local manager appointed under the company's Commercial Registry must appear physically before the bank's KYC officer. Foreign directors may execute an irrevocable Power of Attorney at the Egyptian Consulate or provide apostille signatures; the appointed local agent must then attend the bank interview. Remote verification via video conference is permitted only for natural-person clients in narrowly defined emergency circulars, but has not been extended to corporates with foreign shareholders. Practical benchmark: physical attendance of a signature-verified board representative accelerates account opening from 10 to 3 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders holding EGP-dominated capital structure without a physical office in Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized and legalized shareholder resolution, a lease or virtual-office contract for an Egyptian registered address, the Company's Article of Incorporation containing the full beneficial ownership chain, and a beneficial-owner declaration signed under penalty of perjury. Include foreign shareholding passports and proof of residency, plus a board resolution stating the capital contribution will be effected via bank transfer from a regulated licenced financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI voice-cloning and subtitle post-production business lacks a sector-specific license, causing uncertainty about revenue source legitimacy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain a written legal opinion from an Egyptian licensed attorney confirming that the business is not within the scope of set licensing requirements of the Supreme Council for Media Regulation (Law No. 17/2018); attach a copy of the company's Commercial Registry with ISIC code 5912, two executed client contracts, sample invoices with accurate purpose codes, and the technical report of the AI/audio pipeline demonstrating that it processes copyright-clean source materials. Keep a notarized copy of all standard vendor IP indemnification clauses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume credit-card transactions via Stripe and Wise generated from foreign clients without supporting import/export documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce the Stripe/Wise account statements showing the settlement currency and underlying payment descriptions, the merchant agreement, and a transaction-level breakdown mapped to late-payment invoices. Provide the bank's specific anti-fraud questionnaire response confirming the company does not handle commodities or services on the Egyptian prohibited-import list. Include a screenshot-free summary of the PSP's own AML measures and a declaration by the compliance officer of the bank confirming the transaction source is valid.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a non-resident shareholder's capital injection into EG_LLC: (i) the electing bank must receive the SWIFT MT103 from the shareholding entity's corporate account with a clear remitter name matching the shareholder register; (ii) the message must carry the statutory purpose code 'Equity Capital Contribution' (CBE internal code EB-01) or 'Shareholder Loan' (EB-05); (iii) the company must upload to the bank's electronic portal the CBE 'Inward Remittance Application' (Form A), a copy of the Commercial Registry extract, and a board resolution confirming the injection; (iv) the bank will perform a cross-match of the CBE Central Bank registry to verify the remitter is not on an anti-money-laundering sanction list. If the contribution exceeds USD 100,000, the bank may request the original notarized board minutes and a certificate of capital contribution from the company's auditor. Funds are released to the EGP capital account or USD convertible account within 48 hours of documentary approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for trade payables related to production, subcontracting, and licensing will primarily execute via SWIFT MT103 for B2B supplier invoices under a purchase order designated with the Egyptian Customs' import code '579' (software and AI-assisted media content). For disbursements exceeding USD 50,000, the CBE-compliant alternative is a Domestic Commercial Letter of Credit at sight, issued in favor of the non-resident supplier, requiring (i) the commercial invoice, (ii) a bill of lading or delivery certificate, and (iii) the form 'Import Requisition' from the Ministry of Trade. All transfer cables must include the ultimate beneficial owner of the beneficiary to ensure downstream correspondent banks do not reject the instruction. Royalty and license fee outflows are cleared after the tax office's confirmed withholding tax deposit with the transfer code 'D-7' (royalties).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Egyptian Pound forward (DF) with a maturity of up to one year, executed through a CBE-authorised dealing bank and supported by an underlying trade invoice.
Cross-currency swap (CCS) for foreign-currency denominated shareholder loans or equipment finance, requiring CBE descriptive filing and a valid debt schedule.
Egyptian Pound profit-rate swap (implemented as a currency margin hedge) for fixing variable-rate obligations, subject to CBE anti-speculative margin limits.
FX spot contracts for same-day liquidity conversion when exact payment dates are aligned due to invoice maturity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Declaration (Article 49, Income Tax Law No. 91/2005)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Income Tax Department; regional tax office of record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer the return is due by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional tax per Article 132 of Law 91/2005 plus a fixed penalty where no tax is due; willful non-filing is a misdemeanor under Article 133 with fines and possible imprisonment; enforced collection follows via tax lien and asset seizure; non-filing for two consecutive years supports GAFI administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, auditor’s report, and management report deposited with the companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department / One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer the ordinary general assembly and the deposit are due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the accounting and statutory books provisions is punishable by fines under Law No. 159/1981 of up to EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,040); two consecutive years without filed audited statements allow the Commercial Registry to administratively strike the LLC off and initiate dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration renewal (Trade Register, Law No. 34/1976)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry; where applicable, the GAFI One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, during the month corresponding to the anniversary of the original commercial registration; most Egyptian LLCs renew during January–March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal is subject to a fine of EGP 200–1,000 (approx. USD 5–20); when renewal lapses beyond the anniversary month the commercial registration is involuntarily closed, preventing import/export, blocking bank compliance, and making the entity subject to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GAFI annual corporate dues and annual file renewal certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Companies Affairs Department / GAFI Treasury
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March of each calendar year or the anniversary date stated on the GAFI registration certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment incurs a monthly surcharge of approximately 0.5% on the unpaid fee, suspension of the renewal certificate and GAFI-issued licenses; prolonged delinquency causes administrative closure and strike-off of the company file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation derived from audited accounts (monthly VAT returns are already due separately under Law No. 67/2016)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal reconciliation is assessed and resolved within the annual tax declaration cycle due 4 months after year-end; monthly VAT returns remain due by the end of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT returns/reconciliation attract an addition of 2% of the VAT due for each month of delay, minimum EGP 500 and maximum 100% of the liability; serial non-filing triggers a field audit, seizure of assets, suspension of the tax card, and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Assembly approval of annual financial statements and annual register-confirmation record (shareholding movement confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – company file; notary public in cases of share transfers requiring authentication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Assembly must be convened and the financial statements approved within 6 months after year-end; share transfers and ownership changes must be registered with GAFI within 30 days of the movement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the assembly exposes directors/managers to fines under Law No. 159/1981; title transfers not recorded in the register are unenforceable against third parties and recurrent failures may cause GAFI to classify the LLC as inactive and proceed to deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No de minimis exemption applies to Egyptian LLCs. Every LLC must appoint at least one ETA-registered independent statutory auditor (Article 107, Companies Law No. 159/1981), irrespective of turnover or balance-sheet size; the audit is mandatory for all LLCs and applies equally to the AI media/post-production entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued under Ministry of Finance Decree No. 110/2015 and largely converged with IFRS; full IFRS is used for banks, financial institutions, and consolidated groups; EAS is the mandatory statutory framework for EG_LLC tax and GAFI filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt does not operate a stand-alone annual UBO registry return. Beneficial ownership is instead captured through the annual GAFI corporate-file renewal, the Commercial Registration records, AML Law No. 80/2002 customer-due-diligence rules, and the mandatory internal Register of Members. For this EG_LLC, the manager confirms annually by 31 March that the member/UBO register remains accurate; any share transfer or amendment must be notarized, filed with GAFI within 30 days, and reflected contemporaneously in the statutory books.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–1,800 per year for a registered office address or an authorized corporate service agent in Cairo/GAFI-administered zones
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 900–2,500 per year for a low-volume post-production LLC; fee rises if cross-border licensing or transfer-pricing documentation is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% standard Egyptian corporate income tax rate for juridical persons (Law No. 91 of 2005, Art. 8, as amended by Law No. 96 of 2015); branches of foreign companies are taxed at the same 22.5% on Egypt-source profits attributable to a permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) licensed projects may qualify for a 0% CIT holiday of up to 15 fiscal years from the commencement of activity, subject to actual economic substance and ETA certification; the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits eligible projects in development areas to deduct up to 50% of investment costs from taxable profits over a specified incentive period (generally 7 years); small and micro enterprises with annual gross turnover not exceeding EGP 20 million may elect a presumptive turnover-based tax of 0.4% to 1.5% of gross revenue under Law No. 30 of 2023; free-zone entities licensed by GAFI benefit from 0% CIT on export-oriented post-production, dubbing and AI subtitle services; the default headline rate for an Egyptian LLC inside the ordinary regime remains 22.5%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 10 for juridical persons, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal accessible via www.eta.gov.eg and the associated incometax.gov.eg digital services platform; the annual transfer pricing disclosure module is submitted together with the same income tax return using the ETA digital certification of the tax representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; three provisional CIT instalments are payable during the tax year and the final balance is settled with the annual return; the ETA may require quarterly estimated accounting in cases of deferred filing or non-resident ownership with irregular distributions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form No. 10 must be filed within four months after the close of the fiscal year (Law No. 91 of 2005, Art. 65); an Egyptian LLC using a calendar fiscal year must file by 30 April of the following year; a written extension can be requested from the ETA before the statutory date and is granted only for exceptional reasons.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The LLC name, ETA tax card number, GAFI (General Authority for Investment) registration number, head office address, fiscal year, reporting currency and the accounting standards applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must appoint a resident tax representative or agent before first filing; the representative must be identified in the return and hold a notarized and Arabic-translated power of attorney accepted by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Revenue and Egyptian-source income disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross invoiced income from automated subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning, audio dubbing, software licensing, streaming platform royalties and SaaS subscriptions; deferred revenue is recognized in accordance with Egyptian GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income attributable to a fixed place of business or services performed in Egypt is taxable in Egypt; Stripe, Wise, PayPal and other payment rail settlements must be reconciled to Egypt-source invoices and converted into EGP at the Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate on the recognition date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Deductible expenditures and arm's-length adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct linguist, voice artist and subcontracting costs, studio rental, software and server costs, licenses, salaries, social insurance, utilities and depreciation; entertainment expenses, tax penalties and related-party fees exceeding arm's-length value are disallowed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent company recharges for AI models, software development or management services must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; payments for access to overseas voice libraries are reviewed for royalty characterization and the existence of a hidden service PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of tax losses carried forward from prior years, limited to five consecutive fiscal years following the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is forfeited where more than 50% of the LLC ownership changes and the principal purpose is tax avoidance; the ETA applies a continuity-of-business test and may deny losses of a dormant shell entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Withholding tax credits and final taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for 10% dividend withholding tax and 20% royalty or interest withholding tax suffered at Egyptian source; final taxes on separately taxed investment income are reconciled in this section.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only tax actually remitted to the ETA is creditable; a non-resident claiming a treaty-reduced rate must attach the ETA relief approval to avoid double taxation and refund delay.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Taxable income and headline rate computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of adjusted taxable profit after statutory deductions and incentive relief, followed by application of the 22.5% headline CIT rate and subtraction of provisional instalments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ETA checks thin capitalization where shareholder loans exceed commercially justifiable debt-to-equity levels; interest exceeding the acceptable ceiling is recast as a constructive dividend subject to 10% WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing gives rise to a delinquency fine under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 86 of 2023 (fixed monetary penalties scaled for juridical persons and supplemented by monthly incremental fines until the return is submitted); late payment continues to attract the statutory 2% monthly surcharge on the tax due (Law No. 91 of 2005, Art. 134); false statements may result in an ETA estimated assessment, an additional tax penalty of up to 100% of the understated tax and criminal referral of the responsible managers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-resident juridical persons without a permanent establishment in Egypt (Law No. 91 of 2005, Art. 56); resident Egyptian corporate shareholders are generally exempt from dividend WHT where the distributing company has fully settled its CIT; a non-resident individual shareholder is also subject to the 10% final dividend tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a withholding tax relief application to the ETA before the distribution date, attaching the current home-country Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) authenticated by the relevant competent authority and translated into Arabic, duly legalized constitutional documents, an updated share register excerpt, a beneficial ownership declaration and a legal analysis of the applicable DTA article; the ETA assesses the substance and tax residence of the claimant; upon approval the reduced rate is communicated to the paying company and its bank for immediate application; if the ETA refuses the reduction, the payer must withhold the domestic 10% rate and the non-resident may pursue a refund claim within the statutory limitation period by resubmitting the treaty documentation and proof of Egyptian WHT settlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis WHT for non-residents is 20% on royalties, technical fees, management fees and charges for using or licensing intangibles such as subtitle software, AI voice models and audio dubbing libraries (Law No. 91 of 2005, Art. 58); interest on shareholder loans and debt instruments paid to non-residents is subject to 20% WHT, with lower decree-based rates applicable to bank interest and listed bonds; Egypt's double tax agreements generally reduce royalty WHT to 10%-15% and interest to 10%-15%, while technical service fees may remain taxable at 20% unless the DTA treats them as business profits without a PE; the treaty rate is accessible only with a valid TRC and after the ETA beneficial ownership check.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Egyptian TP Guidelines (Ministerial Decree No. 81 of 2021 implementing Art. 30 bis of Law No. 91 of 2005), the annual transfer pricing disclosure must be filed with the CIT return where the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds EGP 4,000,000 during the tax year or where the taxpayer's annual gross revenues exceed EGP 20,000,000; at or above these thresholds the taxpayer must prepare and maintain a contemporaneous Local File and, for multinational group structures, a Master File; both files must be produced to the ETA within 30 days of a written request; transactions below the thresholds still require reasonable arm's-length support but are not subject to mandatory file preparation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (comparable uncontrolled price) method, preferred for voice licensing, subtitle software sales and routine AI processing contracts where comparable third-party prices exist
Resale price method, suitable for a local LLC acting as a distribution reseller of studio services and platform rights
Cost plus method, applied to the Egyptian post-production service company where its costs are the most reliable functional basis
TNMM (transactional net margin method), typically appropriate for a routine dubbing and AI subtitle processing entity with limited risk and functional profile
Profit split method, used for integrated development of proprietary AI voice models and jointly held intellectual property with cross-border value contribution
